These are synthetic three-page PDFs generated with pypdf. Page two is blank;
page three contains `unlockcanarythird` so extraction can verify original page
numbers after decryption. The PDFs contain no user documents or credentials.

| File          | Encryption   | User password           | Owner password           |
| ------------- | ------------ | ----------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `rc4-40.pdf`  | RC4, 40 bit  | `fixture-user-password` | `fixture-owner-password` |
| `rc4-128.pdf` | RC4, 128 bit | `fixture-user-password` | `fixture-owner-password` |
| `aes128.pdf`  | AES, 128 bit | `fixture-user-password` | `fixture-owner-password` |
| `aes256.pdf`  | AES, 256 bit | `암호-fixture-密碼`     | `fixture-owner-password` |

These public passwords are deliberately test data. Application tests copy the
PDFs into disposable authorized folders and verify that processing leaves the
original encrypted bytes unchanged. No decrypted PDF is written by the app.

`generate.py` regenerates the files with the independent `pypdf` and
`cryptography` Python packages. AES encryption intentionally uses fresh random
data, so regenerated bytes and hashes differ; text, passwords and page numbers
remain the same. These packages are not runtime dependencies of Prism.
